name: Manoj Ceramic Ltd
title: Manoj Ceramic Ltd - 544073 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Manoj Ceramic is a distributor-led B2B/B2C tile seller with no owned capacity; H2 FY26 EBITDA margin fell to about 11% from 14% and management gave no quantified FY27 margin path.

summary.headline: Manoj Ceramic FY26 total income rose 23.4% to ₹202.99 cr, but EBITDA was flat at ₹24.88 cr and H2 EBITDA margin fell to ~11% from ~14%.
summary.overview: Management reported FY26 total income up 23.4% YoY to ₹202.99 cr, with PAT up 10.1% to ₹12.01 cr and EBITDA of ₹24.88 cr. H2 FY26 total income grew 23.3% to ₹120.82 cr, with EBITDA of ₹13.45 cr and PAT of ₹6.14 cr. Management tied the H2 margin compression to lower-margin tile volumes and service/project contracts with discounts, and said the margin would recover in FY27. Balance sheet metrics improved: debtor days fell from 163 to 114, trade receivables were about ₹63 cr, and long-term borrowings fell from ₹28.98 cr to ₹13.89 cr.

segments.name: B2B
segments.commentary: Management said B2B is about 80-82% of sales, with B2C the balance. B2B is served through a West and South zone logistics network covering more than 900 dealers.

segments.name: B2C / Retail
segments.commentary: Six premium experience centres cover over 1,26,500 sq ft with more than 1,000 SKUs. Management described B2C as a small but growing contributor, supported by the Italian/imported marble division (Marmi Bella).

segments.name: Service / project supply and fixing
segments.commentary: The company said this business carries lower margins but higher volumes, and volume-linked discounts were passed on. This was cited as the main driver of H2 margin compression.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: A Dubai display centre was launched in FY26. Management is targeting African markets, with export operations expected to be operational in the first six months of FY27. No export contribution figure was given.

guidance_outlook: Management reiterated a 25-30% CAGR growth target, saying it has been met since listing and will be pursued in FY27.
Margin recovery is expected in FY27 from premium products, exports and the reduction of low-margin service contracts. Management declined to quantify FY27 or FY28 EBITDA margins.
Working capital discipline is to be tightened further in FY27. No specific debtor or inventory day targets were given.
Management said Capex and expansion plans are on schedule, but gave no amounts and promised announcements later.
capex_capacity: Upper Thane cutting and polishing facility is operational and is the first step toward backward integration.
A new technology-based product launch that was scheduled has been delayed in production and is now expected in FY27.
Management said new depots, new products and new horizons are scheduled, but gave no capex quantum or timeline.
Management did not disclose FY27 or FY28 capex, store expansion counts or capacity figures.
demand_pricing: Volumes were up roughly 23-24% overall, per management. The company said it met its planned volumes despite the Iran-war gas supply disruption in the Morbi cluster.
Prices were raised in the last 15-20 days of March 2026 to pass on the cost impact to customers.
Exports have not been affected because Middle East exposure is limited, according to management.
Management said higher-volume service contracts required discounts, which lowered margins in H2.

qa_highlights.question: Why did H2 EBITDA margin fall about 300 bps to ~11% from ~14%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed new design tile products that drove volume but not sustainable margins. It described the arrangement as temporary and said margins would improve once a delayed new technology product launches in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Has the Iran war and gas supply disruption hurt volumes or margins in March-May?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said volumes met plan and prices were raised in late March to pass on costs. It agreed the position was fine 'so far' and gave no quantified impact for April or May.

qa_highlights.question: What is the receivables ageing, and were all warrants converted?
qa_highlights.answer: Management deferred the ageing breakdown to the public balance sheet. It confirmed all warrants have been converted, including the last one held by the promoter group.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EBITDA bridge and steady-state margin, given EBITDA was flat YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the gap to service/project contracts with lower margins and higher volumes, which required discounts. It declined to quantify FY27-28 EBITDA margins.

qa_highlights.question: What is the B2B/B2C mix and aspirational direction?
qa_highlights.answer: B2B is about 80-82% of sales. Management said it will stay B2B-led while building B2C through word of mouth, the Italian marble division and experience centres.

qa_highlights.question: How does the asset-light model compare with manufacturers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management argued that sourcing from multiple manufacturers avoids machinery capex and depreciation, and that its logistics network lets it take up new products within about 15 days.

risks_watch: H2 EBITDA margin ~11% vs ~14% last year, and FY26 EBITDA broadly flat at ₹24.88 cr despite 23% revenue growth. Watch whether FY27 margins recover.
Gas supply disruption in the Morbi cluster from the Middle East conflict. Management says it is so far unaffected, but pricing was raised and the position may change.
Operating cash flow was about -₹35 cr per the analyst, and management did not address it. Receivables ageing is undisclosed.
A delayed technology product launch and a dependence on third-party manufacturers for supply and new products.
Export ramp-up in Africa and the GCC is still at an early stage and has no quantified targets.
summary.management_tone: Confident and promotional on growth, with repeated 25-30% CAGR commitments. Evasive on specifics: margin, receivables ageing, FY27 capex and H2 margin bridge were deferred or not quantified.
key_quotes: We have increased the volumes by about 23-24% roughly overall.

So we have already announced that the CAGRs of 25 to 30% have has been maintained before right from our first earning call after getting listed and we have kept the promises and the promise keeps on continuing in the same manner.

EBITDA margin ~11% vs ~14% in H2 FY25 (per analyst; not disputed by management)

financial_highlights.value: Analyst cited about -₹35 cr; not addressed by management

adds.what: Upper Thane cutting and polishing facility (operational; first step toward backward integration)
New technology-based product launch (production delayed, now expected in FY27)

growth.why: Management reiterated a 25-30% CAGR target for FY27 (midpoint 27.5%) but gave no capex amounts, capacity figures, or FY27 margin quantification; the Upper Thane facility is operational, the new product is delayed to FY27, and export (Africa) ops are expected in the first six months of FY27 with no contribution figure, so backing is vague.
